## Overview

This report presents the Pearson correlation between RNA and protein log2 fold‑change values for genes measured in both transcriptomics and proteomics layers.

## Load Correlation Data

```{r load-data}
cor_file <- file.path(config$output$output_dir, "tables", "rna_protein_correlations.csv")
if (!file.exists(cor_file)) {
  stop("Correlation file not found: ", cor_file)
}
cor_df <- read.csv(cor_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

## Summary Statistics

```{r summary}
summary_stats <- data.frame(
  n_genes = nrow(cor_df),
  mean_cor = mean(cor_df$correlation),
  median_cor = median(cor_df$correlation),
  sd_cor = sd(cor_df$correlation),
  n_positive = sum(cor_df$correlation > 0),
  pct_positive = 100 * sum(cor_df$correlation > 0) / nrow(cor_df)
)
knitr::kable(summary_stats, caption = "Correlation Summary")
```

## Correlation Distribution

```{r plot, results='asis'}
# Check existence using R's working dir (project root)
real_path <- file.path(config$output$output_dir, "plots", "rna_protein_correlation.png")
if (file.exists(real_path)) {
  # Output relative path for Pandoc (running in reports/)
  cat("![](../outputs/plots/rna_protein_correlation.png)\n")
} else {
  # Fallback: generate on the fly
  ggplot(cor_df, aes(x = correlation)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", color = "white", alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = "RNA‑Protein log2FC Correlation Distribution",
         x = "Pearson Correlation", y = "Count")
}
```

## Top Correlated Genes

```{r top-genes}
top_genes <- cor_df %>% arrange(desc(abs(correlation))) %>% head(20)
knitr::kable(top_genes, caption = "Top 20 Genes by Absolute Correlation")
```
